review_summary: The differential captures the major cardiometabolic issues but mis‑weights several probabilities and omits a dedicated pro‑thrombotic/platelet activation diagnosis. Adjusted probabilities better reflect the strength of evidence. Key missing investigations (lipids, renal work‑up, polysomnography details, iron studies) limit certainty. Overall reasoning quality is good but requires refinement of probabilities and addition of a few targeted work‑ups.
